clue.text: Time to regret being faithful?

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether staying loyal is something they will come to regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A true friend is a loyal, steadfast one, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Knotted garter to make instrument for executioner

indicators.note: something knotted is twisted and tangled up, so the letters lose their original order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A twisted garter is improvised into a weapon for a hangman.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrotte is a cord or wire used to strangle a condemned prisoner, an execution device.

clue.text: Approach director before the beginning of Yorick's amusing performance

indicators.note: before tells us the earlier pieces are placed ahead of the next one in order

parts.note: to approach is to come towards
D is a common abbreviation for director

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the initial letter of the name

explanation.surface: A theatrical note: a director steps in just before the jester Yorick's funny turn in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorick is the dead jester whose skull Hamlet holds, which makes the theatrical surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a play or show written to make an audience laugh.

clue.text: Rough sea, for me, is daunting

indicators.note: rough water is churned up and disordered, just as these letters are thrown about

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A nervous sailor admits that stormy waters frighten them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fearsome inspires dread, so it is intimidating or daunting; the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Conservative wearing badge in charge of alfresco dining

indicators.note: a person wearing a badge has it on them, so the badge word goes around the other

parts.note: a pin is a small badge fixed to clothing
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A Tory wearing an official badge is put in charge of eating outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is a meal eaten outdoors, and alfresco means in the open air.

clue.text: Put up with tedious character

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tolerated, the past tense of bear
second meaning: a dull, tiresome person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as present tense, but it is past here, matching the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of bear means endured or tolerated, and the noun is a person who wearies others.

clue.text: Smart reasons to conceal crime

indicators.note: the words conceal the answer within them, so it sits inside the run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary of these two words

explanation.surface: Clever excuses are offered to cover up wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country or sovereign, is among the gravest crimes.

clue.text: Meat cooked in ovens

indicators.note: cooking transforms its ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A plain kitchen statement: meat roasted in ovens.
explanation.definitionFit: Venison is the flesh of deer eaten as food, a particular kind of meat.

clue.text: Vegetable with right to become a fruit

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A vegetable claims it has the right to be reclassified as a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet orchard fruit, so this is a specific example of the general class.

clue.text: Staying power needed to finish university career, gaining first in nanotechnology

indicators.note: a word gaining something takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the finish is the end
U is the abbreviation for university
to career is to rush along, to race

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Stamina is required to complete a university career in nanotechnology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about working life, but it is the verb meaning to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the capacity to keep going under strain, which is what staying power describes.

clue.text: Source of nutritional advice to pass on to old master

parts.note: to pass on is a euphemism for to die
Titian was a great Venetian Renaissance painter, an old master

explanation.surface: Someone seeking diet tips must pass the advice along to an elderly Renaissance painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a health professional who advises people on what to eat.

clue.text: Daft place to do a wee

definitions.meaning: first meaning: silly or crazy, informal British
second meaning: a child's chamber pot used for toilet training

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like the Scots word for small, but here it means urination.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal adjective means mad, and the noun is a small pot a toddler uses as a toilet.

clue.text: Nip back to church in an emergency

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so this word is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: In a crisis, someone nips back to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nip' tempts as a definition, since a nip is a pinch, but it is the word to turn around.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch is a critical situation, as in the idiom 'at a pinch', meaning if absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Crucifix finally found during cries to arrange for a priest with special powers …

indicators.note: a thing found during another sits in the middle of it, so it goes inside
to arrange is to put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A crucifix is found amid screams, and someone is told to send for a priest, as in a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into 15 across, but each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An exorcist is a cleric with the authority to drive out evil spirits, a special power.

clue.text: Girl's witty remark

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a quick, clever retort

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s reads as possessive but stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common female name and also a noun for a lively quip or witticism.

clue.text: … formerly working with church

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, the priest used to work for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adverb means at some time in the past, the same sense as formerly.

clue.text: Assistant covering up second remark that's not for everyone's ears

definitions.text: remark that's not for everyone's ears

indicators.note: covering something up means wrapping round it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: an aide is an assistant
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An assistant hushes up a second confidential comment.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage an aside is a line spoken so only the audience hears, not other characters.

clue.text: Fat cat about to ruin item of historical interest

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks its shape, so these letters fall into a different order

parts.note: the letters taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A wealthy businessman is about to wreck a precious antique.
explanation.walkthrough: A fat cat is a slang name for an overpaid boss.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a man-made object, typically one studied by historians or archaeologists.

clue.text: Good antique metal

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
antique things are old

explanation.surface: A fine piece of old metalwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is a precious yellow element, one example of a metal.

clue.text: German's mature and sensible — and down to earth

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a rounded personality is fully developed, mature

explanation.surface: A description of a German who is grown-up, level-headed and unpretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives the answer once, and it fits both definitions: level-headed, and literally brought back down to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded person is realistic and level-headed, and a grounded aircraft is kept on the ground.

clue.text: Bread, tea and portion of butter upset Italian

parts.note: cha is a British slang word for tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down-or-across light that reads the word backwards

parts.note: It is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Bread, tea and a dab of butter have displeased an Italian guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapatti is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: Experiment with pot in food store

indicators.note: with here places the second item alongside, so the pot comes first and the trial follows

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
to experiment is to try something out

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a new pot in the larder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where food is kept.

clue.text: Animal eating Kew's centrepiece plant

indicators.note: an animal eating something takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

indicators.note: the centrepiece of a word is its middle letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the three-letter name

explanation.surface: A beast munches the prize plant at Kew Gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London, which fits the plant theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A peony is a garden plant grown for its large showy flowers.

clue.text: Ample number to host a full meeting

indicators.note: to host is to hold within, so the answer lies inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the boundary of these two words

explanation.surface: A large enough number of people to hold a full assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is an assembly attended by all members, a plenary session.

clue.text: To guarantee money for a specific purpose call receiver

definitions.text: To guarantee money for a specific purpose

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: A finance instruction: secure the funds, then phone the receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' suggests a telephone handset next to 'call', but it is the criminal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To ringfence funds is to protect them so they can only be spent on one designated purpose.

clue.text: Kingdom losing large pieces of paper

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a realm is a kingdom
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A kingdom is short of big sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper, five hundred sheets.

clue.text: Medical advisory body is discriminating

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the UK's National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
second meaning: subtle, fine in distinction

explanation.walkthrough: NICE is the British body that rules which treatments the NHS should fund. 'Discriminating' sounds negative, but means finely precise.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names the UK health agency, and the older adjective means precise or subtle.

clue.text: Pretend not to notice dieter's third sweet

parts.note: to cut someone is to snub them, ignoring them deliberately

indicators.note: the third of a word is its letter in position three, so only that is kept

parts.note: the letter in third position of the word

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet ignores the third dessert on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means charming and endearing, the same sense as sweet applied to a child or puppy.

clue.text: Express disapproval of army accommodation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to jeer or heckle
second meaning: a building where soldiers live

explanation.walkthrough: The plural is usual for soldiers' quarters, but the singular is a fair attributive noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to shout scornfully at a speaker, and a barrack block houses troops.

clue.text: Somewhere to get drunk with English royal reaching extremely tricky time of life

parts.note: a pub is a bar
E is the abbreviation for English
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, its two outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A drinking den with an English royal arriving at an awkward age.
explanation.definitionFit: Puberty is the stage of adolescence when the body matures sexually, a period in one's life.
